cards.title: The American Revolution
body: The American Revolution (1775-83), arose from growing tensions between residents of Great Britain’s 13 North American colonies and the colonial government, which represented the British crown.

cards.title: Background: Britain and its thirteen colonies
body: **Great Britain.** The United Kingdom of Great Britain was formed in **1707** when England and Scotland united. In the 18th century its trade and industry grew, creating a growing middle class that wanted more trade and a bigger empire.
**William Pitt the Elder** (head of the cabinet from 1757) expanded the empire by winning **Canada and India** in the Seven Years' War.
**The colonies.** Britain ruled Canada and **13 colonies** on the east coast of today's USA. By 1750 they had more than one million people and were prosperous.

**How they were governed.** In theory by the Board of Trade, the Royal Council and Parliament; in practice the colonies had their own **legislatures** that usually acted independently, so for 150 years they grew with little interference.
**Key idea.** The revolution began when Britain tried to end this self-rule after 1763.
**Memory trick:** "1707 union, 1750 one million, 1763 trouble begins."

cards.title: Model answer: what the American Revolution was
cards.problem: (Short answer) What was the American Revolution and who were the two sides?

steps.text: Sides: residents of Great Britain's 13 North American colonies against the colonial government, which represented the British crown.
Cause in one line: growing tensions over taxes and lack of representation.
Result: an independent United States, recognised by Britain in the Treaty of Paris (1783).

cards.answer: The American Revolution (1775–83) was the struggle of Britain's 13 North American colonies against the British crown, ending in the independence of the United States.

cards.title: Causes of the Revolutionary War
body: Attempts by the British government to raise revenue by taxing the colonies (notably the Stamp Act of 1765, the Townshend Acts of 1767 and the Tea Act of 1773)
lack of representation in Parliament

cards.title: The causes, step by step
body: **Step 1 – the end of "leave them alone".** For over 150 years Britain let the colonies develop freely.
**Step 2 – war debt.** After the Seven Years' War (1756–63) Britain needed money to pay war costs and an army to defend the colonies.
**Step 3 – the Stamp Act (1765).** Legal documents and newspapers had to carry a stamp showing a tax was paid; violent opposition forced its cancellation in 1766, but the dispute was not resolved.

**Step 4 – the Tea Act (1773).** A British company got the right to sell tea directly, cutting out colonial merchants; Bostonians dressed as Native Americans dumped the tea into the harbour – the **Boston Tea Party**.
**The principle.** "No taxation without representation" – the colonists had no members in Parliament, so they denied its right to tax them.
**Memory trick:** "Debt → Stamps → Tea → Revolt."

cards.title: Model answer: causes of the American Revolution
cards.problem: (Exam question) Explain the causes of the American Revolutionary War.

steps.text: Taxation: Britain tried to raise revenue by taxing the colonies – Stamp Act (1765), Townshend Acts (1767), Tea Act (1773).
Representation: the colonists had no representatives in Parliament – "no taxation without representation".
Trade restrictions: British rules limited colonial trade.
Escalation: the Boston Massacre (1770) and the Boston Tea Party (1773) led to the Intolerable Acts and open conflict.

cards.answer: British taxes and trade restrictions imposed without colonial representation, made worse by events in Boston, caused the war.

cards.title: Boston massacre 1770
body: Colonial resistance led to violence in 1770, when British soldiers opened fire on a mob of colonists, killing five men in what was known as the Boston Massacre.

cards.title: The Boston Massacre: what happened and why it mattered
body: **Background.** British troops were sent to Boston to enforce the new taxes (the Townshend duties of 1767 on goods such as glass, paper and tea). Their presence caused daily friction with townspeople.
**The event (5 March 1770).** A crowd taunted and threw snowballs and stones at a group of British soldiers guarding the customs house; the soldiers fired, killing **five** colonists.
**Propaganda.** Patriots called it a "massacre" and spread pictures of soldiers shooting peaceful citizens, which turned many colonists against Britain.
**What followed.** Most Townshend duties were cancelled, but the **tax on tea** remained, which led to the Tea Act crisis and the Boston Tea Party (1773).
**Why it matters for the exam.** It is an example of how violence and propaganda pushed the colonies from protest towards revolution.
**Memory trick:** "1765 stamps, 1770 shots, 1773 tea."

cards.title: Boston tea party (immediate cause)
body: After December 1773, when a band of Bostonians altered their appearance to hide their identity boarded British ships and dumped 342 chests of tea into Boston Harbor during the Boston Tea Party.
An outraged Parliament passed a series of measures (known as the Intolerable, or Coercive Acts) designed to reassert imperial authority in Massachusetts.

In response, a group of colonial delegates met in Philadelphia. This First Continental Congress did not go so far as to demand independence from Britain, but it denounced taxation without representation, as well as the maintenance of the British army in the colonies without their consent. It issued a declaration of the rights due every citizen, including life, liberty, property, assembly and trial by jury. The Continental Congress voted to meet again in May 1775 to consider further action, b
The Revolution.

cards.answer: The Tea Party provoked the Intolerable Acts, which united the colonies in the First Continental Congress and led directly to war.

cards.title: Declaring Independence (1775-76)
body: When the Second Continental Congress convened in Philadelphia, delegates—including new additions Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson—voted to form a Continental Army, with Washington as its commander in chief.

On June 17, in the Revolution’s first major battle, colonial forces inflicted heavy casualties on the British regiment of General William Howe at Breed’s Hill in Boston. The engagement, known as the Battle of Bunker Hill, ended in British victory, but lent encouragement to the revolutionary cause.

By June 1776, with the Revolutionary War in full swing, a growing majority of the colonists had come to favor independence from Britain. On July 4, the Continental Congress voted to adopt the Declaration of Independence, drafted by a five-man committee including Franklin and John Adams but written mainly by Jefferson.

**Step 3:** So the answer is B) Thomas Jefferson.

lessons.title: Saratoga: the American revolution Turning Point (1777-78)

cards.title: Saratoga: the American revolution Turning Point (1777-78)
body: The British suffered the consequences of this on September 19, when an American force under General Horatio Gates defeated them at Freeman’s Farm in the first Battle of Saratoga.

After suffering another defeat on October 7 at Bemis Heights (the Second Battle of Saratoga), Burgoyne surrendered his remaining forces on October 17. The American victory Saratoga would prove to be a turning point of the American Revolution, as it prompted France (which had been secretly aiding the rebels since 1776) to enter the war openly on the American side, though it would not formally declare war on Great Britain until June 1778. The American Revolution, which had begun as a civil conflict between Britain and its colonies, had become a world war.

cards.title: Why Saratoga was the turning point
body: **Military.** A whole British army under Burgoyne surrendered (17 October 1777), proving that the Americans could defeat regular troops.
**Diplomatic.** France, which had secretly supplied arms and money since 1776, openly recognized the USA in **February 1778** and entered the war; Spain and the Dutch Republic followed.
**Result.** Britain now had to fight much of Europe as well as the Americans.
**Memory trick:** "Saratoga brought France."

cards.problem: (Exam question) Explain why the Battle of Saratoga was the turning point of the American Revolution.

steps.text: The battles: American forces under Horatio Gates won at Freeman's Farm (19 September) and Bemis Heights (7 October 1777).
Surrender: Burgoyne surrendered his remaining forces on 17 October 1777.

Result: a colonial civil conflict became an international war against Britain.

cards.answer: Saratoga ended with Burgoyne's surrender and brought France openly into the war, turning a colonial revolt into an international war Britain could not win.

cards.title: The End of the Revolution (1781-83)
body: The British removal of their troops from Charleston and Savannah in late 1782 finally pointed to the end of the conflict. British and American negotiators in Paris signed preliminary peace terms in Paris late that November, and on September 3, 1783, Great Britain formally recognized the independence of the United States in the Treaty of Paris.

cards.title: Foreign help, Yorktown and the Treaty of Paris
body: **Why the Americans won although Britain was stronger.** Britain was a great military power with huge finances; the Continental Army was made of short-term amateur soldiers. Foreign help made the difference: France gave arms, money, officers and soldiers, then recognized the USA in 1778; Spain and the Dutch Republic joined the war against Britain.
**Yorktown (1781).** The British army surrendered to combined American and French forces under **George Washington**, and Britain decided to end the war.
**The Treaty of Paris (3 September 1783).** Britain recognized the independence of the United States and gave the Americans control of the western territory.
**Memory trick:** "France + Washington = Yorktown 1781; Paris 1783 = freedom."

cards.title: Impact of the American Revolution
body: At the meeting known as the convention meeting in Philadelphia in in 1787 55 delegate from all states agreed to write a new constitution and federal government with three branches (Legislative, Executive and judiciary) was formed. The legislative had two houses the senates and House of Representatives.
The revolution had also weak side it failed to free the blacks and women’s right was not improved.

cards.title: From Articles of Confederation to the Bill of Rights
body: **Articles of Confederation (1781).** The states feared strong central power, so the national government was too weak to solve the new nation's problems.

**Constitution (1787).** It created a **federal system** sharing power between national and state governments, with **checks and balances** between the three branches; nine states had to ratify it, and George Washington became the first president.
**Bill of Rights (1789–91).** Congress proposed 12 amendments; the 10 approved guaranteed freedom of religion, speech, press, petition and assembly – rights drawn from Enlightenment ideas.
**Wider impact.** Europeans saw the revolution as Enlightenment ideas made real; it inspired the French Revolution and Latin American independence movements.
**Memory trick:** "Weak Articles → Strong Constitution → Ten Rights."

cards.title: Model answer: impact of the American Revolution
cards.problem: (Exam question) Discuss the positive and negative impacts of the American Revolution.

steps.text: Positive 1: an independent United States with a written constitution (1787 Philadelphia convention, 55 delegates).
Positive 2: a federal government with three branches (legislative, executive, judiciary) and a two-house legislature (Senate and House of Representatives).
Wider effect: it inspired other revolutions, notably the French Revolution.
Negative: it failed to free black slaves and did not improve women's rights.

cards.answer: It created an independent, constitutional republic with separated powers and inspired others, but left slavery and women's inequality untouched.

questions.q: 42. Declaration of Independence of America was written by:
questions.label: 13. 42. Declaration of Independence of America was written by:
why: Answer E: Thomas Jefferson

From the lesson: “When the Second Continental Congress convened in Philadelphia, delegates—including new additions Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson—voted to form a Continental Army, with Washington as its commander in chief.”
**Thomas Jefferson** was the principal author of the Declaration of Independence, adopted by the Continental Congress on July 4, 1776.
So the answer is E) Thomas Jefferson.
